mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate reduces the cost of capital for corporations, increasing the present value of future cash flows and leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS < 3.5% is followed by negative 20-day S&P 500 returns in more than 60% of the months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in the Consumer Price Index above 0.5% per month signals an acceleration in inflation, prompting the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, which increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is positive in more than 60% of the months when CPIAUCSL rises by more than 0.5% over 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in employment (PAYEMS) and industrial production (INDPRO) indicates robust economic expansion, which typically leads to higher corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and INDPRO both rise > 0.1% in 1 month
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is negative in more than 60% of the months when both PAYEMS and INDPRO increase by more than 0.1% in 1 month.

mechanism_narrative: In high inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 5% annualized), the Federal Reserve is likely to implement aggressive monetary tightening, which increases real interest rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is positive in more than 60% of the months when CPIAUCSL > 5% annualized.

mechanism_narrative: A high level of housing starts (HOUST) indicates strong consumer demand for residential real estate, which is a leading indicator of economic expansion and corporate revenue growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: HOUST > 1500 is followed by negative 20-day S&P 500 returns in more than 60% of the months.

mechanism_narrative: A low unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a tight labor market, which can lead to wage inflation and force the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: UNRATE < 3.5% is associated with positive 20-day S&P 500 returns in more than 60% of the months.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of strong GDP growth (GDPC1) and elevated inflation (CPIAUCSL) signals an overheating economy, which typically triggers aggressive monetary tightening by the Federal Reserve, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward return is positive in more than 60% of the months when GDPC1 annual growth > 1.5% and CPIAUCSL > 3.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A strong level of retail sales (RSAFS) indicates robust consumer spending, which is a key driver of corporate revenue and earnings growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: RSAFS > 700000 is followed by negative 5-day S&P 500 returns in more than 60% of the months.
